Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}x+y, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}(x+y)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-2,2]\times [-1,1]$
- $R=[0,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$

authoring.value:
The displayed region has points above $y=1$, so rectangle I, whose vertical range is $[-1,1]$, does not contain all of $D$. The region also has points with $x<0$, so rectangle II, whose horizontal range is $[0,2]$, does not contain all of $D$. The entire drawn region lies in rectangle III, $[-2,2]\times[-2,2]$.

For rectangle III, $f=x+y$ on $D$ and is zero on $R\setminus D$. Therefore $\iint_R f\,dA=\iint_D(x+y)\,dA$. Only III meets the explicit containment requirement, giving "III only".
